title: Seven Days and a Garden
bigQuestion: What does the first story in the Bible say about how the world began?

story.title: The Biggest Book in the House
story.kicker: Grandma opens a very big book to page one, and a story begins.
paragraphs: Mia's grandma keeps a very big book on the shelf. It is heavy. It has thin pages and a soft cover. On Sunday, Grandma lifts it down. She sets it on the table. She opens it to page one.
"This book is called the Bible," Grandma says. "It is really many books inside one cover. The first one is called Genesis. Genesis means beginning." Mia looks at the small words. There are so many.
Grandma reads slowly. The story says God made light. Then sky. Then land and sea. Mia listens. She likes the part about the fish and the birds. She likes the part about the animals even more.

"Jewish people and Christian people both tell this story," Grandma says. "Some people read it one way. Some read it another way. Tonight we will just listen to what it says." Mia nods. She wants to hear about the garden.
story.think: What is the first thing you would want to hear about in a story about the beginning of the world?

lessons.title: One Cover, Many Books
lessons.mainIdea: The Bible is one big book made of many smaller books.
reading: The *Bible* looks like one book. But it is really many books. Each small book has its own name. They sit together inside one cover, like books on a shelf.
The small books have different kinds of writing. Some tell stories. Some are songs. Some are letters. Some are lists of rules. People have read them for a very long time.
Christians count 66 books in most of their Bibles. Jewish people read the first part and count it as 24 books. The words are the same. People just count them in different ways.

words.d: a big book made of many smaller books, read by Jews and Christians

look.title: Counting the Books
look.cite: Book counts of the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Which part has more books, the Old Testament or the New Testament?

choices: One big book made of many smaller books
check.why: The Bible is many small books kept together inside one cover.

check.q: What kinds of writing are inside the Bible?
check.why: The small books hold many kinds of writing: stories, songs, letters and rules.

choices: Jewish people and Christian people, and many others
check.why: Jews and Christians read the Bible. Many other people read it too.

lessons.title: The First Story
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis is the first book, and it starts with a story about the beginning.
reading: The first book in the Bible is called *Genesis*. Genesis means beginning. It starts with a story about how the world began. The story says God made everything.
In this class we say "the story says." We are learning what is in the book. Jewish people tell this story. Christian people tell it too. They read it in their own ways.
You can tell the story too. You do not have to believe it to learn it. You just need to listen and remember what it says.

words.d: the first book of the Bible; its name means beginning
a telling of what happened, in order, from start to end

look.title: Two Readers, One Story
look.text: Look at a big table. On one side, a Jewish family reads Genesis on Saturday in Hebrew. On the other side, a Christian family reads Genesis on Sunday in English. The words tell the same story. Each family listens in its own way.
look.prompt: What is one thing the two families do the same? What is one thing they do differently?

check.q: What does the name Genesis mean?
check.why: Genesis means beginning. It is the first book, and it tells about the start of the world.

check.q: Which book comes first in the Bible?
check.why: Genesis is the very first book in the Bible.

check.q: In class, how do we talk about the story?
choices: We say it is not true
We say everyone must believe it
check.why: In a public school we learn what the story says. We do not tell anyone what to believe.

lessons.title: Light, Sky, Land and Sea
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God made light, sky, land and sea in the first three days.
reading: Genesis begins in the dark. The story says God spoke. "Let there be light." And there was *light*. That was day one.
On day two, the story says God made the sky. On day three, God made dry land and the sea. Then plants and trees grew on the land.
Each day in the story ends the same way. There was evening, and there was morning. Then a new day begins.

words.d: what lets us see; the story says it came on the first day

look.title: The First Words God Says
look.text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
look.prompt: In the story, what happens right after God speaks?

check.q: What does the story say came on day one?
check.why: Genesis 1 says light came first, on day one.

check.q: What does the story say God made on day three?
check.why: Day three is land, sea and plants in the story.

check.q: How does the story say God made things?
check.why: The story says God spoke, and things came to be.

lessons.title: Sun, Fish, Animals and Rest
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God made sun, moon, fish, birds, animals and people, then rested.
reading: On day four, the story says God made the sun, the moon and the stars. On day five, God made fish for the sea and birds for the sky.
On day six, the story says God made the animals. Then God made *people*, a man and a woman. The story says God looked at it all. It was very good.
On day seven, the story says God *rested*. Nothing new was made. Many Jewish people rest on Saturday because of this. Many Christians rest on Sunday.

words.d: human beings; the story says they were made on day six
stopped working; the story says God rested on day seven

look.title: What Came on Each Day
look.prompt: Which day comes first: fish and birds, or sun and moon?

check.q: What does the story say God made on day five?
check.why: Day five is fish and birds in Genesis 1.

check.q: What does the story say happened on day seven?
check.why: On the seventh day, the story says, God rested from all the work.

check.q: When were people made in the story?
check.why: People come on day six, after the animals.

lessons.title: A Garden Called Eden
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God put the first people in a garden called Eden with one rule.
reading: Genesis tells about a garden. Its name is *Eden*. The story says God planted it. It had rivers and trees with good fruit.
The first man is called *Adam*. The first woman is called *Eve*. The story says they lived in the garden. They took care of it.
There was one rule. The story says they could eat from any tree but one. That tree was in the middle of the garden.

words.d: the garden in the Genesis story where the first people lived
the first man in the Genesis story
the first woman in the Genesis story

look.title: Picture the Garden
look.text: Look at a green garden. A river runs through it. Trees hang heavy with fruit. Birds sing. In the middle stands one tree that is not for eating. Adam and Eve walk past it every day.
look.prompt: Why do you think a story would put one rule in a place with so much to enjoy?

check.q: What is the garden in the story called?
check.why: The garden in Genesis 2 is called Eden.

check.q: Who lived in the garden in the story?
check.why: Adam and Eve are the first people in the Genesis story.

check.q: What was the one rule in the story?
choices: Do not eat from one tree
Do not drink from the river
check.why: The story says one tree in the middle was not for eating.

lessons.title: The Snake and the Fruit
lessons.mainIdea: The story says a snake talked, the rule was broken, and the people left the garden.
reading: The story says a *snake* came to Eve. It could talk. It said the fruit was good to eat. Eve ate some. She gave some to Adam. He ate too.
Now the rule was broken. The story says Adam and Eve hid. God asked what they had done. Then they had to leave the garden.
Jewish people and Christians read this part in different ways. Many Christians call it "the fall." Many Jewish readers see a story about choosing. Both keep telling it.

words.d: the animal in the story that talks Eve into eating the fruit
something you must do or must not do

look.title: Leaving the Garden
look.text: The story says God sent Adam and Eve out of the garden of Eden. Now they would work the ground to grow their food.
look.cite: Genesis 3:23, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: How do you think Adam and Eve felt as they walked out of the garden?

check.q: Who talked to Eve about the fruit in the story?
check.why: Genesis 3 says a snake spoke to Eve about the fruit.

check.q: What happened after the rule was broken?
choices: Adam and Eve left the garden
Adam and Eve built a boat
check.why: The story says Adam and Eve had to leave Eden.

check.q: How do Jews and Christians read this story?
choices: Only one of them reads it
In their own ways, and both keep telling it
check.why: Both traditions tell the story. They read it in their own ways.

choices: Many small books in one cover
review.why: The Bible is a set of many books kept together.
Genesis comes first, and its name means beginning.

review.q: What does the story say came on day one?
review.why: Genesis 1 says God said, Let there be light, on day one.

review.q: What does the story say God did on day seven?
review.why: The story says God rested on the seventh day.

review.q: Where did Adam and Eve live in the story?
review.why: The story puts Adam and Eve in the garden of Eden.
Both Jews and Christians tell the Genesis story, each in their own way.
